title: More details, please. The case for Australian SSNs is incomplete | The Strategist
paragraphs: The Australian government still has some explaining to do on the AUKUS submarine program. Two of the stated reasons for buying nuclear attack submarines (SSNs) – deterrence and trade protection – have holes in them.
This is not to say they are necessarily false. But the public needs more details about a program that’s estimated to cost as much as A$368 billion over 30 years.

And, on the point of money, that needs explaining, too. We have not heard a thorough explanation from the government of why buying SSNs is preferable to buying other equipment, such as aircraft, or economic security measures, such as subsidising domestic production.
